nodes.title: Artist
nodes.body: The artist is the central creative business whose songs, performances, image, and choices give the whole team a direction.

details.whatTheyDo: Creates and performs the work, approves major opportunities, and makes the career choices the team supports.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Every deal, campaign, tour, and release exists to grow the artist's audience and income.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: The artist is involved from the first creative idea through release, promotion, touring, and long-term brand decisions.
details.exampleDecision: Deciding whether to release a single independently, sign with a label, or hold the song for a larger rollout.

nodes.title: Artist Manager
nodes.body: The artist manager is the day-to-day strategist who turns creative goals into business priorities and keeps the team aligned.

details.whatTheyDo: Coordinates the professional team, filters opportunities, manages timelines, and helps set the artist's long-term strategy.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: A manager protects the artist from scattered decisions and makes sure business moves support the bigger career plan.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They usually become central once an artist has momentum, offers, releases, or touring activity that needs coordination.
details.exampleDecision: Choosing whether a brand offer fits the artist's image or distracts from the next release.

nodes.title: Songwriter & Composer
nodes.body: Songwriters and composers create the lyrics, melodies, and musical ideas that become the copyright behind a song.

details.whatTheyDo: Write or co-write the composition and help shape the emotional and musical identity of the record.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Strong songs create long-term value through publishing income, covers, sync placements, and repeat listening.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They are involved before or during recording, especially in writing sessions, toplining, and arrangement development.
details.exampleDecision: Splitting writing credit fairly after several collaborators contribute hooks, lyrics, and melodies.

nodes.title: Music Producer
nodes.body: The music producer guides the sound of the recording and helps turn a song idea into a finished master.

details.whatTheyDo: Shapes arrangements, performances, sounds, session flow, and creative choices during the recording process.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: A producer can make the record feel commercially competitive while still matching the artist's identity.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter during pre-production and recording, often before the engineer captures the final takes.
details.exampleDecision: Choosing whether a track needs a live drummer, a programmed beat, or a simpler arrangement.

nodes.title: Audio Engineer
nodes.body: The audio engineer captures, mixes, and masters recordings so the final track sounds polished and release-ready.

details.whatTheyDo: Runs recording sessions, edits takes, balances the mix, and prepares masters that meet platform standards.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Good engineering keeps a strong song from sounding unfinished, unclear, or uncompetitive next to other releases.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They are involved during studio recording, mixing, mastering, and final delivery checks.
details.exampleDecision: Deciding whether the vocal needs another take, more editing, or a different mix approach.

nodes.title: Entertainment Attorney
nodes.body: The entertainment attorney protects the artist's rights and negotiates the contracts behind deals, releases, and touring.

details.whatTheyDo: Reviews deal terms, negotiates contracts, explains legal risk, and protects ownership, royalties, and approvals.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Music deals can affect income and control for years, so artists need someone focused on legal leverage.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They should be involved before signing label, publishing, management, producer, licensing, or live performance agreements.
details.exampleDecision: Negotiating whether a label deal gives the artist enough creative control and a fair royalty structure.

nodes.title: Business Manager
nodes.body: The business manager handles the artist's money, budgets, taxes, and financial planning as the career becomes more complex.

details.whatTheyDo: Tracks income and expenses, pays bills, manages taxes, reviews budgets, and helps plan sustainable growth.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Artists can look successful publicly while losing money privately if touring, advances, and taxes are not managed.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They become important when income grows, touring costs rise, or multiple royalty streams need tracking.
details.exampleDecision: Checking whether a proposed tour is profitable after crew, travel, production, commissions, and taxes.

nodes.title: Music Publisher
nodes.body: The music publisher manages song rights, collects publishing income, and looks for licensing opportunities for compositions.

details.whatTheyDo: Registers songs, collects publishing royalties, pitches music for sync, and helps manage composition rights.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Publishing can create income long after release through radio, streaming, covers, samples, and film or TV placements.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter once songs are written, released, licensed, or valuable enough to administer professionally.
details.exampleDecision: Deciding whether to approve a TV placement based on fee, exposure, and fit with the artist's image.

nodes.title: A&R Executive
nodes.body: The A&R executive connects artists with label resources and helps guide creative development inside the record company.

details.whatTheyDo: Finds talent, supports song selection, connects artists with producers, and advocates for projects inside the label.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: A strong A&R partner can help an artist get attention, resources, and creative support from the label.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They are involved during signing discussions, recording, release planning, and label decision-making.
details.exampleDecision: Choosing which single to push first based on the artist's sound, audience, and label priorities.

nodes.title: Marketing & PR Representative
nodes.body: Marketing and PR representatives shape public attention around the artist, the story, and each release.

details.whatTheyDo: Plans campaigns, pitches media, coordinates social strategy, manages press moments, and supports audience growth.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Even strong music can get lost without a clear story, release plan, and way to reach listeners.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter before a release, tour, announcement, or public moment that needs coordinated attention.
details.exampleDecision: Choosing whether to lead a campaign with a music video, playlist pitch, press story, or social rollout.

nodes.title: Booking Agent
nodes.body: The booking agent secures live opportunities, negotiates performance fees, and helps turn audience demand into shows.

details.whatTheyDo: Books concerts, festivals, and appearances while negotiating fees, routing, holds, and live deal terms.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Live shows build fan relationships and income, but poor routing or weak deals can waste time and money.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They become important once an artist can sell tickets, support bigger acts, or attract festival interest.
details.exampleDecision: Deciding whether to accept a lower-paying support slot because it reaches the right audience.

nodes.title: Concert Promoter
nodes.body: The concert promoter presents the live event, sells tickets, markets the show, and takes on much of the local financial risk.

details.whatTheyDo: Rents or works with venues, markets the show, manages ticket sales, and settles the event finances.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Promoters connect artists to local audiences and determine whether a show is financially realistic in a market.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter when a booking agent is placing dates or negotiating individual concert offers.
details.exampleDecision: Setting ticket price and venue size based on expected demand, artist fee, and marketing budget.

nodes.title: Tour & Production Manager
nodes.body: The tour and production manager turns a live plan into a workable road operation with budgets, schedules, crew, and equipment.

details.whatTheyDo: Coordinates travel, schedules, production needs, crew communication, technical riders, and day-to-day tour logistics.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: A tour can fail financially or operationally if timing, staffing, equipment, and budgets are not controlled.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter once live dates are being planned and become central as rehearsals and the tour approach.
details.exampleDecision: Choosing whether a larger lighting package is worth the cost for the venues on the route.

nodes.title: Live Technical Crew
nodes.body: The live technical crew makes the show work on stage by handling sound, monitors, instruments, lighting, and gear.

details.whatTheyDo: Sets up equipment, runs front-of-house and monitor sound, maintains backline, and supports the performance each night.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: The audience judges the live experience, and the crew helps make the artist sound and look professional.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter during rehearsals, load-in, soundcheck, the performance, and post-show breakdown.
details.exampleDecision: Solving a monitor problem before doors open so the artist can hear clearly on stage.

nodes.title: Digital Distributor & Platform Gatekeeper
nodes.body: Digital distributors deliver releases to streaming platforms, while platform gatekeepers can influence discovery and playlist reach.

details.whatTheyDo: Sends music and metadata to platforms, manages delivery requirements, and supports pitches for platform visibility.
details.whyArtistNeedsThem: Listeners cannot find a release if the music, credits, artwork, and timing are not delivered correctly.
details.whenTheyGetInvolved: They enter before release day when metadata, artwork, audio files, and pitch timelines must be finalized.
details.exampleDecision: Choosing a release date that gives enough time for playlist pitching and clean platform delivery.

edges.label: career strategy
edges.body: The artist and manager coordinate the professional team, long-term strategy, and business priorities around the artist's career.

edges.label: studio collaboration
edges.body: Studio collaboration to record masters and realize the project's sonic vision.

edges.label: creative co-authorship
edges.body: Creative co-authorship of lyrics and melodic compositions.

edges.label: creative development
edges.body: Creative development and internal advocacy for the artist within a record label.

edges.label: live booking
edges.body: Securing and planning live appearances and tour routes.

edges.label: legal protection
edges.body: Legal protection through negotiation of label and performance contracts.

edges.label: financial oversight
edges.body: Financial oversight, including bill payment and tax planning.

edges.label: public image
edges.body: Development of public image and media strategy for consumer outreach.

edges.label: road logistics
edges.body: Daily road logistics, travel coordination, and show scheduling.

edges.label: stage support
edges.body: Direct support for sound, lighting, and instrument readiness on stage.

edges.label: label alignment
edges.body: Strategic alignment of the artist's output with label release schedules.

edges.label: release rollout
edges.body: Execution of marketing rollouts and social media engagement plans.

edges.label: tour timing
edges.body: Collaboration on tour timing and selection of key live markets.

edges.label: deal review
edges.body: Vetting of new business offers for legal risks and contract finalization.

edges.label: sustainable growth
edges.body: Coordination to ensure career growth is financially sustainable.

edges.label: royalties and sync
edges.body: Tracking royalty collections and identifying synchronization opportunities.

edges.label: tour supervision
edges.body: High-level supervision of tour staffing and operational budgets.

edges.label: producer matching
edges.body: Scouting and matching specific producers to the artist's project.

edges.label: deal structure
edges.body: Legal structuring of signing deals and sample clearance agreements.

edges.label: recording and mix
edges.body: Directing the technical recording and mixing process for sonic quality.

edges.label: arrangement refinement
edges.body: Refinement of song arrangements and structures during production.

edges.label: song administration
edges.body: Administrative management of song copyrights and royalty payouts.

edges.label: metadata and placement
edges.body: Ensuring song data reaches supervisors and playlist curators for placements.

edges.label: sync publicity
edges.body: Integrating high-profile song placements into PR campaigns.

edges.label: appearance deals
edges.body: Negotiation of artist appearance fees and event deal terms.

edges.label: riders and schedules
edges.body: Exchange of technical riders and logistical tour schedules.

edges.label: show settlement
edges.body: Financial settlement and reconciliation of show revenue at the venue.

edges.label: ticket campaign
edges.body: Promotion of local events and coordination of ticket sales campaigns.

edges.label: venue staffing
edges.body: Linking touring needs with local venue security and stagehands.

edges.label: playlist traction
edges.body: Pitching to editors and influencers for playlist and social traction.

edges.label: technical standards
edges.body: Verification that master recordings meet platform technical standards.

edges.label: royalty audit
edges.body: Audit of label royalty statements and tracking of recoupable advances.

edges.label: contract economics
edges.body: Financial assessment of contract clauses and long-term royalty impacts.

edges.label: road budget
edges.body: Management of road budgets, crew payroll, and tour-related taxes.

edges.label: daily show operation
edges.body: Daily direction of equipment setup, safety, and live operation.
